findings.title: Perception before naming
findings.claim: The opening places the addressee's recognition before the civilization is named.
findings.mechanism: The carrier a-lam tara precedes the final bi-Adin phrase, so the hearer's readiness to recognize the event becomes the first semantic step before its historical case appears.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader feels the summons arrive before the name it asks them to recognize.
findings.containment: The named people and the completed action remain the ordinary referents; the finding concerns their order of presentation.

epistemic.reason: The focus word order and supplied prior-address support directly establish the relation.

findings.title: Rhetorical summons
findings.claim: The ayah opens as a rhetorical summons that presses toward recognition.
findings.mechanism: The interrogative and past-negating particle complex a-lam governs tara with jussive force; the negative question therefore directs the hearer toward an expected recognition rather than a neutral information request.
findings.reader_payoff: The first words sound like a challenge addressed to someone expected to see.
findings.containment: The finding describes the force of the question and does not add a separate event or change the historical report.

epistemic.reason: QAC, attachment, and translation-support records agree on the particle's government and rhetorical force.

findings.title: Grammatical pressure before content

findings.mechanism: The rootless a-lam complex combines interrogation, negation, and jussive government before tara, so the reader enters the ayah under grammatical pressure rather than through a bare statement.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah's first movement is already an act of address.
findings.containment: This concerns the opening form; it does not turn the particles into an additional lexical event.
